title: The Contact of the DMZ
premise: Hazel Villalobos, a private security contractor guarding a data sanctuary straddling the Korean DMZ, discovers that a voiceprint in her own client files unlocks a server in Frankfurt holding evidence of a sanctioned massacre covered up by the firm that employs her. Hunted by both the company's fixers and the intelligence service that trained her, Hazel must decide whether to sell the archive to a whistleblower collective or expose it publicly and lose her only leverage for survival. With help from the ragtag sanctuary staff she's come to call family, she smuggles the evidence out during a staged evacuation, trades the secret to the collective in exchange for testimony that dismantles the firm, and chooses exile over redemption — but not before sending the massacre's architect to face justice outside any courtroom.
about_author: Hazel Marchetti is a former risk analyst who spent a decade consulting for security firms before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse in the Dolomites, drawing on the moral gray zones of the private security world she left behind.

chapters.title: Perimeter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She runs a routine security sweep of the DMZ sanctuary, establishing the rules-bound rhythm of her life and her wary affection for the staff — medic Sun-woo, archivist Petra, and teenage intern Milo. When a client's encrypted file pings her voiceprint from Frankfurt, the beat is unease: the machine knows her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She replays the access log and realizes the server contains footage of the Kassala massacre — an operation her own firm helped bury. Her handler, Reyes, dismisses her questions with chilling calm. Emotional beat: denial curdling into dread as she understands the file was left for her deliberately.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Sun-woo's POV. The sanctuary's daily life fractures as firm auditors arrive unannounced. Sun-woo notices Hazel lying for the first time in three years and quietly covers for her. Emotional beat: loyalty tested — the found family senses the storm before Hazel admits it exists.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in Panmunjom
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She meets an old intelligence contact in the joint security area to verify the footage's authenticity. He confirms it — and warns her that Reyes has already flagged her as a leak. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the institution that trained her now hunts her.

chapters.title: What Petra Kept
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The archivist reveals she's been preserving suppressed testimonies for years and offers Hazel the sanctuary's hidden network. Their alliance deepens into something like sisterhood. Emotional beat: hope — for the first time, Hazel isn't alone with the secret.

chapters.title: The Fixers Arrive
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. The firm's fixers raid the sanctuary under pretext of an inspection, and Milo — the kid Hazel swore to protect — is interrogated. Hazel watches helplessly from the comms room. Emotional beat: protective rage; the cost of her secret lands on the people she loves.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She flies to Frankfurt to broker the archive's sale to the whistleblower collective before markets open, negotiating with their wary leader, Anselm, while Reyes's team closes in. Emotional beat: cold clarity — Hazel accepts she must spend the secret, and perhaps herself, to make it count.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In a bank vault turned negotiation room, Hazel trades the archive for the collective's protection and testimony — then discovers Reyes is the massacre's architect, not just its cleaner. The exchange goes loud. Emotional beat: fury and resolve fused into action.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The climax: Hazel leads the fixers through Frankfurt's underground transit corridors while the collective simultaneously publishes the archive. Reyes corners her; she chooses exposure over execution, broadcasting his confession live. Emotional beat: the terrifying freedom of having nothing left to hide.

chapters.title: After the Markets Close
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, weeks later. The firm collapses, Reyes faces an international tribunal built from the collective's evidence, and Hazel — legally erased, quietly exiled — returns to the sanctuary one last time to say goodbye to her found family. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; justice outside the law, family beyond borders.
